lots.guide_summary: Only close entries are US retail asks for single or paired German bisque figures, A$137 to A$216 (USD at 1.437), which are optimistic. No same-item sold or unsold result. Tasmanian category guide: Gowans sold painted bisque and decorative figure pairs at $2 to $110 hammer (mostly damaged, $25 to $49 typical), two unsold showings of a damaged pair, and blue and white dishes at $35 to $40.
lots.working: No SOLD result for the same figures or a comparable set of four plus an onion dish in similar condition, so keep 0 and flip 0 under the rules. Context only: local results suggest two undamaged bisque pairs plus a decorative onion dish would make perhaps $60 to $130 hammer at Gowans; the US asks are retail and well above what the Tasmanian room pays. A crossed swords Meissen mark on the dish would change this.
lots.confidence_reason: No maker's mark read on figures or dish (bases and back not photographed); all price evidence is category guide or asking.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the LiveAuctioneers item 237177522 (six Bavarian onion plates, est. US$300 to $350) as evidence: snippet only, page blocked, currency unconfirmed; it is a lead only. Downgraded the five Gowans entries the researcher called 'close' (395048, 393487, 369974, 439440, 424355) to category guide: they are different, mostly larger or damaged figures, not this set. Moved the Chairish 38 cm pair (US$450) to category guide (much larger). All Gowans records were re-opened and titles, hammer and bid counts match the researcher.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos. Painted script titles on the sailor bases: 'Distress' read clearly (photo 3 enlarged); the fisherman's reads '...cue' at the end, probably 'Rescue', so the two men are likely a titled pair. Smaller boy with mandolin and girl in bonnet and striped apron form a second pair. Pastel matt bisque with no obvious breaks; fingers and the sailor's raised cloth look intact at this resolution. Dish: scalloped rim, onion pattern, handwritten inventory number on the rim ending '142'. No undersides photographed, so no marks.
lots.condition: Looks good in the photos, no breaks seen; small chips or restorations cannot be ruled out. Sizes not stated.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any marks or numbers under the dish (crossed swords, Meissen, Bavaria, a maker's name) and under the figures? Is the second fisherman's base titled 'Rescue'? Any chips, cracks or restoration, especially to fingers, the raised cloth and the mandolin? What are the heights and the dish diameter?
